title: Chapter 38: Underground Parking Lot
html:
Uncle Xu was telling him all this because he genuinely cared. “Knowing that, do you still want to put money into the Haunted House?”

“I still want to try. The new park hasn’t opened yet, and New Century Park isn’t gone yet.” Chen Ge’s real confidence came from the black phone, but that was not something he could explain.

“You’re usually a sensible kid, so why are you so stubborn about this?” Uncle Xu sighed. “I’ve worked here for ten years. I want the park to survive too. But wanting something doesn’t change the numbers.”

He gestured toward several attractions that were already closed. “People say they failed safety inspections, but most simply cost more to operate than they earn. Years ago, the park was so crowded that the surface lots overflowed and we had to borrow parking from nearby businesses. We eventually built an underground lot to handle the demand. For the last three years, even on holidays, we haven’t needed it. Attendance has kept dropping, and this year is the worst yet.”

“Wait. You said the underground parking lot hasn’t been needed for three years. So it’s basically unused?” A new idea lit Chen Ge’s eyes, immediately making Uncle Xu suspicious.

“Pretty much. When the park first opened, the place was packed and every attraction had long lines. Those were good years.” Uncle Xu smiled faintly. “At least we had them.”

“How much would it cost to rent the underground parking area?”

“What?” Uncle Xu stared at him. “Why are you asking that?”

The answer had already become obvious in Chen Ge’s mind. He had found the space he needed. “If the lot is sitting unused, why not let me convert part of it for the Haunted House?”

“Have you lost your mind? Why would you want to rent that place—to raise bats?” Uncle Xu stared at him as though the question itself proved something was wrong.

There was no point hiding his plans when park management would eventually notice. “I want to expand the Haunted House. Financially, the underground parking area makes sense. It isn’t being used, the rent should be lower than a finished building, and the enclosed environment already suits the attraction.”

“A three-story Haunted House isn’t enough work for you? Do you know how large that parking area is? Even if management rented it to you, by the time you finished converting it, the park might already be closed.” Uncle Xu shook his head. “Stop chasing impossible projects and focus on the business you have.”

“I’m serious, Uncle Xu.”

“So am I.” Uncle Xu switched his walkie-talkie back on and headed toward the crowd. A few steps away, he turned. “I’ll bring you the five thousand tomorrow morning. But keep your feet on the ground, all right?”

“I know.” Chen Ge followed him, looking at the crowd outside his attraction. “For what it’s worth, visitor numbers certainly haven’t gone down. Not long ago I was lucky to get any customers at all.”

After squeezing through the onlookers, Chen Ge addressed the students. “Recovered yet? If you stay sprawled here much longer, people are going to think I did something terrible to you.”

“Give me a few more minutes. Your Haunted House takes time to digest.”

“Why is everyone staring at me? I’m fine. I just twisted my ankle in there, that’s all.”

“Every stranger looks suspicious to me now. What did that place do to my brain?”

“Stop pretending we didn’t lose,” Monkey said, finally getting to his feet. He held up the five-star review he had just posted. “But don’t think this is over. We’re not surrendering forever.”

“So you’re coming back tomorrow?”

“We have exams tomorrow,” Monkey said quickly. “Otherwise, obviously, we’d accept the challenge.” His pale face and unsteady legs made the boast less convincing.

“My doors are always open if any of you want another attempt.” Chen Ge was beginning to regard the Jiujiang Medical University students as a personal good-luck charm.

“I am never coming back,” He San muttered. “You would have to carry me through that door.” The eye staring through the crack had clearly left an impression.

“Careful saying things like that around this place,” Xiao Hui said as He San helped her stand. She glared at Chen Ge. “You’re the first man who has ever made me cry hard enough to ruin my makeup. I’m going to remember you.”

Noticing the bump on the back of her head, Chen Ge decided against teasing her. The students started toward the park entrance together. Just when he thought they had gone, Brother Feng returned alone. “I’ve been thinking about your question. I still can’t believe what happened was supernatural. There has to be some explanation involving perception, stress, or suggestion.”

Chen Ge knew exactly what he meant. “Maybe. By the way, I never got your full name.”

“He Feng. I’m a little older than most of them, and I’ll be starting my residency soon.”

“Good to meet you properly. I have a feeling we’ll run into each other again.”

After exchanging numbers, Chen Ge returned to the Haunted House, closed the gate, and hung a Temporarily Closed for Maintenance sign outside.

“Boss, there are still people waiting. Why are we closing?” Xu Wan asked.

“There’s a safety issue I need to deal with first. Could you explain it to the remaining customers?” Chen Ge changed out of the Doctor Skull-Cracker costume, gathered more black fabric from the props room, and returned to Murder by Midnight.

He covered every mirror he could find, but the scenario contained so many rooms that he quickly ran out of fabric.This place is too large. Until we have better monitoring and I understand what happened, I’m not putting visitors back in here.

He locked the scenario and returned downstairs. By then, almost everyone outside the Haunted House had left.

“Xiao Wan, you can take off the stage makeup. We’re done for today.”

After saying goodbye to her, Chen Ge returned to the staff break room. He had barely slept since the previous day and passed out as soon as his head touched the pillow.
